# Product-source incidence and an explicit defect at a circuit contact

This is a contact test for the finite grouped cap certificate. It joins
different original integer fibers through an actual convex representation
of a real contact base. It does not allocate the total mixed mass among
the circuits and does not prove OC.

We use `candidate a25f203b14ed76b3`: if a finite family
of affine halfspaces covers a Euclidean space, its normal span has rank
r>=1, and K is any full-dimensional convex body in that space, then
one cap has at least gamma_r times the volume of K. If all boundaries
have a common affine intersection which misses int K, the stronger
constant is gamma_(r-1), with gamma_0=1. The rank-sensitive theorem is
proved separately by projecting uniform volume to the normal span and
using the continuous projective dimension-drop theorem. The external
rank-one case also follows directly from an interval and its two rays.

## 1. Source and circuit data

Let P be a finite set of distinct integer vectors. For z in P let K_z
be a d-dimensional convex body of volume w_z>0. Suppose their convex
hull is contained in the original body C. All sums and integrals below
use ordinary d-volume on these original fibers.

Fix one positive circuit of ambient caps

  H_j={ (z,x): L_j(z,x):=a_j.z+u_j.x-b_j >=0 },

with u_j nonzero. Its strictly positive multipliers lambda_j satisfy
sum lambda_j=1 and sum lambda_j u_j=0. The continuous normals span V
of rank r. Suppose q=(s,y) is a common boundary contact:

  L_j(s,y)=0 for every j.

Choose distinct source indices z_1,...,z_k and strictly positive
t_1,...,t_k summing to one, such that

  s=sum_l t_l z_l.                                      (1)

Write A=sum_l t_l K_(z_l), a Minkowski interpolant in the real fiber
C_s. Let X_l be independent uniform points of their respective fibers.
The product probability space is uniform volume on the convex body

  K_product=product_l K_(z_l) subset R^(kd).

For every cap define its original fractional source masses

  p_jl=|K_(z_l) intersect H_j,z_l|/w_(z_l),

and its lifted cap probability

  P_j=P{sum_l t_l L_j(z_l,X_l)>=0}.                       (2)

There are no boundary atoms: u_j is nonzero and every source fiber
is full dimensional. In particular all choices of strict versus weak
inequality in these source probabilities agree.

## 2. Exact rank and common-flat geometry

The lifted margins satisfy

  sum_l t_l L_j(z_l,x_l)=u_j.(sum_l t_l x_l-y).            (3)

Their normals are (t_1 u_j,...,t_k u_j), so their span has exactly
rank r. Their strictly positive circuit relation is unchanged.
Consequently their closed caps cover ALL R^(kd), not merely the product
body. Their common boundary flat is

  { (x_l): sum_l t_l x_l belongs to y+V^perp }.            (4)

This flat meets int K_product if and only if

  pi_V y belongs to int_V pi_V A.                        (5)

Indeed the linear map (x_l)->pi_V(sum t_l x_l) is surjective to V.
A surjective linear map sends the interior of a full-dimensional
convex body onto the interior of its image. One elementary proof of
the reverse inclusion is to fix an interior image point produced by
an interior source point; extend the segment from that image point
through the desired interior point slightly within the image, take
any preimage of its farther endpoint, and take the corresponding
strict convex combination with the interior source point.

The rank-sensitive cover theorem therefore gives

  max_j P_j >= gamma_r.                                 (6)

If (5) fails, it gives

  max_j P_j >= gamma_(r-1).                              (7)

No assertion places q in C before (5) has been proved. In the
full-rank case r=d, condition (5) is simply y in int A, and implies
that q lies in C and is interior in its actual continuous fiber.

## 3. Exact union defect, including its strictness

Let E_jl={L_j(z_l,X_l)>=0} and let E_j denote the event in (2).
Because every t_l is positive,

  E_j subset union_l E_jl.

Independence thus gives the exact identity

  P_j=1-product_l(1-p_jl)-Delta_j,                        (8)

where

  Delta_j=P{some L_j(z_l,X_l)>=0,
                  sum_l t_l L_j(z_l,X_l)<0} >=0.          (9)

This defect has a concrete lower certificate. Fix an index i and
positive numbers delta and h_l for l!=i satisfying

  t_i delta < sum_(l!=i) t_l h_l.

Then

  Delta_j >=
    P{0<L_j(z_i,X_i)<delta}
       product_(l!=i) P{L_j(z_l,X_l)<=-h_l}.              (10)

The indicated rectangular event is contained in (9); independence
gives its probability exactly. Thus (10) uses actual cap strips and
opposite tails of the original fibers, not a numerical proxy.

If k>=2, every p_jl<1, and P_j>0, then Delta_j>0. To prove this,
P_j>0 implies p_ji>0 for some i. Hence 0<p_ji<1. An affine functional
with a proper cut through a full-dimensional convex body has positive
volume in every sufficiently small one-sided strip adjacent to that
cut: a segment between interior points on the two sides crosses the
plane at an interior point. For each l!=i, p_jl<1 gives an h_l>0
with positive probability in the negative tail. Choose delta>0
small enough for the displayed strict inequality. Formula (10) is
then strictly positive.

Combining (6) or (7) with (8) yields a finite incidence condition:
for at least one cap j,

  1-product_l(1-p_jl)-Delta_j >= Gamma,                   (11)

where Gamma=gamma_r always, and Gamma=gamma_(r-1) whenever (5)
fails. This is stronger than merely summing original fractional cap
masses. In particular

  sum_l p_jl >= Gamma+Delta_j.

One may additionally keep the exact independent-event overlap
sum p_jl-[1-product(1-p_jl)], which is nonnegative.

## 4. A heavy-fiber hull excludes exterior contacts

Suppose every original ambient cap has total mixed mass at most T,
including all original fibers, and put w_min=min_l w_(z_l). Then

  sum_l p_jl <= T/w_min.                                (12)

If k>=2 and T<w_min, the strictness conclusion above applies to every
lifted cap with positive probability. Therefore (5) must hold whenever

  w_min >= T/gamma_(r-1)                                (13)

and r>=2. Indeed otherwise (7) selects a cap with P_j>=gamma_(r-1),
whereas (8), strict Delta_j>0, and (12) give P_j<T/w_min<=gamma_(r-1).
For k=1 the analogous conclusion holds with strict inequality in (13),
directly from (7). For r=1, the conclusion holds whenever T<w_min:
the exterior rank-one lower bound is one, while every p_jl<1 makes
their finite union probability strictly less than one.

Consequently, for a full-rank circuit, every representation of its
contact base by at least two distinct fibers satisfying (13) forces
its common contact into the interior of their actual Minkowski
interpolant. For a lower-rank circuit it forces the common boundary
flat to meet that interpolant's interior. This is an incidence
constraint across original integer fibers; the real base remains real.

The argument does not replace their discrete volume sum by an integral,
does not change the lattice, and does not infer that a real contact is
a mixed-integer center. Contact bases outside the indicated heavy-fiber
hull are not controlled. Even when every contact is controlled, no
summable allocation of all source fibers among the circuits has been
proved. Those are genuine limits of the statement.

## 5. Exact projected-contact rigidity at the rank threshold

There is a stronger incidence conclusion which uses the unconditional
rank bound (6), rather than the exterior bound. Define the finite set

  P_c={z in P: w_z>=T/gamma_r}.

If the contact base s belongs to conv P_c, it must be a vertex of that
polytope and its own fiber must have volume exactly T/gamma_r.

Indeed a nonvertex s has a convex representation by at least two
distinct points of P_c, all coefficients positive after deleting zero
coefficients. For these sources T/w_min<=gamma_r<1. Equation (6)
selects a lifted cap of probability at least gamma_r, while the strict
defect in (8) and (12) make that probability strictly less than
T/w_min<=gamma_r, a contradiction. A vertex of the finite hull is
one of its defining points. Applying (6) to this single source gives
w_s<=T/gamma_r, hence equality.

In particular no contact base belongs to
conv{z:w_z>T/gamma_r}. The assertion also covers lower-dimensional
finite hulls, using their ordinary definition of an extreme point.
It does not identify a contact outside this heavy-fiber hull or
replace gamma_r by a sum of lighter fiber weights.
